Governed from the fortified port city of Muscat by the Al Said dynasty, the sultanate held authority over coastal Oman, inland desert tribes and overseas enclaves such as Gwadar along the Makran coast. Facing internal Ibadi tribal uprisings and declining maritime trade, the state maintained its sovereign autonomy until concluding exclusive protective treaties with Great Britain in 1892. \n\n Status: Sovereign sultanate; Capital: Muscat; Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Arabic, Balochi and Persian; Religion: Ibadi Islam and Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Al Said; Ruler title: Sultan; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 19 October 1856; Reorganised: 1892; Preceded by: Omani Empire; Succeeded by: Muscat and Oman (British protectorate)

name: Sultanate of Zanzibar
label: polities of the swahili coast
description: The Sultanate of Zanzibar was an independent maritime monarchy established on 19 October 1856 following the partition of the Omani Empire between the sons of Said bin Sultan. Based at Stone Town on the island of Unguja, the sultanate asserted dominion over the fertile clove plantations of the archipelago and an extensive commercial strip along the East African Swahili mainland. The realm prospered on ivory and caravan transit until expanding European imperial competition culminated in the establishment of formal British protection in July 1895. \n\n Status: Sovereign sultanate; Capital: Stone Town; Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Swahili and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Al Said; Ruler title: Sultan; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 19 October 1856; Disestablished: 1 July 1895; Preceded by: Omani Empire; Succeeded by: Zanzibar Protectorate

name: Norfolk Island
label: british colonies in australia
description: Norfolk Island was a self-governing British Crown settlement created on 1 November 1856 following the resettlement of the Pitcairn Island community, composed largely of descendants from the HMS Bounty mutiny. Centred at the historic coastal village of Kingston, the islanders established a unique pastoral democracy guided by local elders and the distinctive Anglo-Tahitian Norfuk language. The island maintained its distinct status under the ultimate supervision of the Governor of New South Wales until being formally transferred to the Commonwealth of Australia on 1 July 1914. \n\n Status: British Crown colony; Capital: Kingston; Official languages: English; Common languages: Norfuk and English; Religion: Anglicanism; Government: Colonial settlement; Ruler title: Chief Magistrate; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1 November 1856; Disestablished: 1 July 1914; Succeeded by: Norfolk Island (Australian territory)

name: Principality of Moldavia
description: The Principality of Moldavia was an autonomous Eastern European state operating under the collective security guarantee of the Great Powers following the evacuation of Austrian peacekeeping forces in 1857. Directed from its cultural and administrative capital at Iași, the principality held robust democratic elections for its ad hoc divan to advocate for administrative modernisation and Romanian political unity. Moldavia's separate statehood culminated on 5 February 1859 when its electors unanimously chose Alexandru Ioan Cuza as prince, sparking the personal union with Wallachia. \n\n Status: Autonomous principality; Capital: Iași; Official languages: Romanian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Elective principality; Ruler title: Hospodar; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1857; Disestablished: 5 February 1859; Preceded by: Principality of Moldavia (Austrian military occupation); Succeeded by: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia

name: Republic of Lydenburg
label: boer states
description: The Republic of Lydenburg was an independent Boer pioneer republic founded across the Mpumalanga highveld of north-eastern South Africa by Voortrekkers seeking autonomy from the Potchefstroom administration. Centred on its capital at Lydenburg, the state functioned through an elected Volksraad that regulated cattle farming, land allocation and frontier trade with Delagoa Bay. After incorporating the neighbouring Republic of Utrecht, the polity voted to terminate its separate existence, formally reunifying with the South African Republic in December 1859. \n\n Status: Sovereign republic; Capital: Lydenburg; Official languages: Dutch; Common languages: Afrikaans and Dutch; Religion: Dutch Reformed Church; Government: Boer republic; Legislature: Volksraad; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1857; Disestablished: 1 December 1859; Succeeded by: South African Republic

name: Yeke Kingdom
description: The Yeke Kingdom was a powerful commercial empire established across the mineral-rich Katanga plateau in modern-day Democratic Republic of the Congo by the Nyamwezi merchant-king Msiri. Governed from the sprawling royal capital of Bunkeya, the monarchy dominated transcontinental trade routes spanning between the Atlantic and Indian oceans, exchanging copper, slaves and ivory for European firearms. The kingdom collapsed abruptly on 20 December 1891 when Msiri was shot during an armed standoff with Belgian officers, leading to the realm's absorption into the Congo Free State. \n\n Status: Sovereign kingdom; Capital: Bunkeya; Common languages: Garanganze and Nyamwezi; Religion: Traditional African religion; Government: Absolute monarchy; Ruler title: King; Head of state: Msiri; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1857; Disestablished: 20 December 1891; Succeeded by: Congo Free State

name: Ballabhgarh State
label: indian princely states
description: Ballabhgarh State was a historic Jat principality situated along the Grand Trunk Road immediately south of Delhi in modern-day Haryana. Established in the eighteenth century by the Tewatia clan with its fortified seat at Ballabhgarh, the realm played a celebrated role in the Indian Rebellion of 1857 under Raja Nahar Singh before being subdued and reorganised under British colonial governance in 1858. The estate retained local hereditary landholdings and civic prestige until the dissolution of princely jurisdictions upon Indian independence in August 1947. \n\n Status: Princely state (under British suzerainty); Capital: Ballabhgarh; Common languages: Hindi and Haryanvi; Religion: Hinduism; Government: Princely estate; Ruling dynasty: Tewatia; Ruler title: Raja; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1858; Disestablished: 14 August 1947; Succeeded by: India

name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
description: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands was a British Crown colony encompassing two isolated coral atolls situated in the eastern Indian Ocean. Formally annexed by Great Britain in 1857 and administered from Direction Island, the territory operated as a feudal copra plantation under the hereditary proprietorship of the Clunies-Ross dynasty while hosting a vital trans-oceanic telegraph cable relay station. The imperial dependency maintained its distinct administrative standing within the British Empire until being officially transferred to Australian sovereignty on 23 November 1955. \n\n Status: British Crown colony; Capital: Direction Island; Common languages: English and Cocos Malay; Religion: Sunni Islam and Christianity; Government: Colonial proprietary administration; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1858; Disestablished: 23 November 1955; Succeeded by: Cocos (Keeling) Islands (Australian territory)

name: Kenglon State
label: shan states
description: Kenglon State was a minor Shan principality situated in the rugged upland valleys of eastern Upper Burma. Established following an administrative partition from Hsenwi State, the realm was governed from its capital at Kenglon by a hereditary Saopha who paid homage and regular tribute to the Burmese royal court at Mandalay. The state maintained internal feudal institutions under Burmese tributary protection until British imperial forces annexed the upper Shan territories in 1886. \n\n Status: Vassal princely state; Capital: Kenglon; Common languages: Shan and Burmese; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Feudal monarchy; Ruler title: Saopha; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1858; Disestablished: 1886; Preceded by: North Hsenwi; Succeeded by: British Burma

name: Kharsawan State
label: indian princely states
description: Kharsawan State was an Odia princely realm situated across the mineral-rich Chota Nagpur plateau of present-day Jharkhand in eastern India. Administered by a branch of the Rathore Rajput dynasty bearing the title of Raja, the state oversaw rich forestlands and agrarian settlements from its capital at Kharsawan under the supervision of the Eastern States Agency. The principality preserved its hereditary internal autonomy until its ruler acceded to the Dominion of India in early 1948. \n\n Status: Princely state (under British suzerainty); Capital: Kharsawan; Common languages: Odia and Ho; Religion: Hinduism; Government: Princely monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Singh Deo; Ruler title: Raja; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1858; Disestablished: 1948; Succeeded by: India

name: Kingdom of Kongo
description: The Kingdom of Kongo was a historic Central African monarchy that entered into formal vassalage and protectorate status under the Kingdom of Portugal in 1858. Governed from its ancient royal capital at São Salvador, the realm was led by the Manikongo, who exercised traditional judicial and ceremonial authority over local chieftaincies under Portuguese military oversight. This protectorate phase persisted until 26 February 1885, when the General Act of the Berlin Conference partitioned the kingdom's lands among European colonial spheres. \n\n Status: Protectorate (under Portugal); Capital: São Salvador; Common languages: Kikongo and Portuguese; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Traditional monarchy under protectorate; Ruler title: Manikongo; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1858; Disestablished: 26 February 1885; Succeeded by: Portuguese West Africa

name: Monghsu State
label: shan states
description: Monghsu State was an upland Shan principality situated in eastern Upper Burma along the fertile basin of the Nam Pang River. Created as a distinct fiefdom following an administrative division of Hsenwi State, the polity was governed from its central town of Mong Hsu by a hereditary ruler loyal to the Burmese Crown. The state maintained its traditional agrarian society and Buddhist monasteries under Burmese overlordship until the British Empire conquered the region in 1886. \n\n Status: Vassal princely state; Capital: Mong Hsu; Common languages: Shan and Burmese; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Feudal monarchy; Ruler title: Myoza; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1858; Disestablished: 1886; Preceded by: Hsenwi State; Succeeded by: British Burma

name: Granadine Confederation
description: The Granadine Confederation was a decentralised federal republic established on 11 April 1858 to succeed the Republic of New Granada across present-day Colombia and Panama. Governed from Bogotá, the constitutional federation granted extensive autonomy to eight constituent states, sparking intense jurisdictional disputes between clerical conservatives and federalist liberals. Plunged into a bitter civil war in 1860, the confederation was dissolved on 8 May 1863 when victorious liberal factions ratified the Constitution of Rionegro to create the United States of Colombia. \n\n Status: Sovereign federal republic; Capital: Bogotá; Common languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Federal presidential republic; Ruler title: President; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 11 April 1858; Disestablished: 8 May 1863; Preceded by: Republic of New Granada; Succeeded by: United States of Colombia

name: British India
description: British India was the vast imperial domain established on 2 August 1858 when the British Crown assumed direct governance over the Indian subcontinent from the East India Company following the Indian Rebellion. Administered initially from Calcutta and subsequently from New Delhi by an imperial Viceroy, the colony oversaw eleven major provinces while exerting paramountcy over hundreds of autonomous princely states. The Raj constructed extensive railway, canal and administrative systems until relinquishing authority during the partition of August 1947 into independent India and Pakistan. \n\n Status: British Crown possession; Capital: New Delhi; Official languages: English; Common languages: Hindustani, Bengali and English; Religion: Hinduism, Islam and Sikhism; Government: Colonial direct rule; Ruler title: Viceroy and Governor-General; Head of state: British Monarch; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 2 August 1858; Disestablished: 15 August 1947; Succeeded by: India and Pakistan

name: Amb State
label: indian princely states
description: Amb State was an autonomous princely realm situated along the Indus River within the rugged Tanawal highlands of modern-day north-western Pakistan. Governed by the Tanoli chieftaincy holding the hereditary title of Nawab, the realm maintained a semi-autonomous status under the British Hazara Tribal Agency without a stationary provincial metropolis. The principality preserved its customary tribal governance and private levies until its rulers signed the Instrument of Accession to the Dominion of Pakistan on 15 August 1947. \n\n Status: Princely state (under British suzerainty); Administrative seat: Mobile court; Common languages: Hindko and Pashto; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Princely monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Tanoli; Ruler title: Nawab; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 15 August 1947; Succeeded by: Pakistan

name: Benna
description: Benna was an autonomous precolonial chieftaincy situated along the coastal river basins of south-western Guinea near the Great Scarcies borderlands. Led by indigenous Susu and Manding chiefs from the settlement of Benna, the polity controlled fertile agricultural river valleys and collected transit tolls from trading caravans bound for Atlantic ports. The chieftaincy preserved its political autonomy until 1892, when French military forces subjugated the coastal kingdoms and incorporated the territory into Rivières du Sud. \n\n Status: Sovereign chieftaincy; Capital: Benna; Common languages: Susu; Religion: Traditional African religion and Islam; Government: Traditional chieftaincy; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 1892; Succeeded by: French Guinea

name: British Concession in Dalian
label: concessions in china
description: The British Concession in Dalian was a temporary military and naval staging enclave established on the southern shores of the Liaodong Peninsula during the Second Opium War. Occupied by the British Royal Navy between 1859 and 1861 to anchor allied fleets preparing for the assault on the Dagu Forts, the outpost supported supply depots and ship repair facilities. The imperial forces relinquished and evacuated this strategic northern maritime position in 1861 following the ratification of the Convention of Beijing. \n\n Status: Military naval concession; Capital: Dabhoi; Common languages: English and Mandarin; Religion: Christianity; Government: Naval military administration; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 1861; Succeeded by: Qing dynasty; Historical region: Concessions in China

name: Buhera
description: Buhera was an autonomous Shona chieftaincy established across the granite plateaus of eastern modern-day Zimbabwe by the VaHera clan. Centred on the traditional kraal at Buhera, the polity was governed by a hereditary paramount leader titled Nyashanu, who oversaw cattle herds, iron forging and regional agricultural trade. The chiefdom maintained its independence from outside imperial control until the British South Africa Company established administrative dominion over the region in 1890. \n\n Status: Sovereign chieftaincy; Capital: Buhera; Common languages: Shona; Religion: Traditional Shona religion; Government: Traditional chieftaincy; Ruler title: Nyashanu; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 1890; Succeeded by: British South Africa Company

name: Cabo San Juan
description: Cabo San Juan was an autonomous coastal enclave established by the Benga people at the promontory of Cape San Juan on the mainland coast of modern Equatorial Guinea. Operating from the port village of Cabo San Juan, indigenous chiefs commanded coastal canoe traffic, bartered timber and palm oil with European ships and defended their sovereign territory from inland expansion. The enclave preserved its political independence until 1886, when Spanish colonial expeditions asserted formal territorial sovereignty over the Río Muni coastline. \n\n Status: Sovereign chieftaincy; Capital: Cabo San Juan; Common languages: Benga; Religion: Traditional African religion; Government: Traditional chieftaincy; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 1886; Succeeded by: Spanish Guinea

name: Corisco
description: Corisco was an independent island kingdom established by the Benga people on the offshore island of Corisco in the Gulf of Guinea. Governed from the settlement of San Roque by traditional monarchs such as King Bonkoro and King Munga, the polity managed island trade networks and accommodated American Presbyterian missions while retaining political autonomy. The kingdom preserved its sovereign standing until 27 June 1900, when the Treaty of Paris formally incorporated Corisco into the Spanish colonial empire. \n\n Status: Sovereign kingdom; Capital: San Roque; Common languages: Benga and Spanish; Religion: Traditional African religion and Protestantism; Government: Traditional monarchy; Ruler title: King; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 27 June 1900; Succeeded by: Spanish Guinea

name: Imamate of Bundu
description: The Imamate of Bundu was a West African Islamic state located between the upper Senegal and Falémé rivers that accepted a French protectorate in 1859. Administered from its fortified citadel at Koundian, the state was ruled by an elected religious monarch known as the Almamy, who maintained Sharia jurisprudence and local executive governance under French colonial surveillance. The protectorate endured until 1906, when French authorities abolished the traditional imamate and integrated its districts into the Colony of Senegal. \n\n Status: Protectorate (under France); Capital: Koundian; Common languages: Fula; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Theocratic monarchy; Ruler title: Almamy; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 1906; Preceded by: Imamate of Bundu (sovereign); Succeeded by: French West Africa

name: Keonthal State
label: indian princely states
description: Keonthal State was a princely principality situated across the scenic pine forests and valleys of the Simla Hill States in northern India. Ruled by a Rajput dynasty from the capital seat of Junga, the realm oversaw twenty-two subordinate feudatories and held significant administrative prominence under the Punjab States Agency. The state governed its mountain communities autonomously until its ruling Raja signed the accession papers in 1948, culminating in its formal integration into Himachal Pradesh in 1949. \n\n Status: Princely state (under British suzerainty); Capital: Junga; Common languages: Western Pahari and Hindi; Religion: Hinduism; Government: Princely monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Rajput; Ruler title: Raja; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 1949; Succeeded by: India

name: Kingdom of Rarotonga
description: The Kingdom of Rarotonga was an independent Polynesian monarchy established across the principal island of the southern Cook archipelago. Administered from the coastal settlement of Avarua, the realm united rival tribal districts under the paramount leadership of the Makea Ariki dynasty in close cooperation with the London Missionary Society. The kingdom enjoyed self-rule under indigenous Christian legal codes until 1889, when rising French imperial influence in eastern Polynesia prompted the monarchy to accept formal British protection. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital: Avarua; Common languages: Cook Islands Maori; Religion: Protestantism; Government: Constitutional monarchy; Ruler title: Ariki; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 1889; Succeeded by: Cook Islands Federation

name: Ongandjera
description: Ongandjera was a sovereign precolonial kingdom established by the Ovambo people across the fertile floodplains of northern Namibia. Centred on the royal palace at Okahao, the realm was governed by a hereditary king bearing the title of Omukwaniilwa, who commanded agricultural production and regional trade in salt, copper beads and iron implements. The kingdom maintained its complete independence and traditional cultural practices until 1896, when German South West Africa extended its colonial sphere northward. \n\n Status: Sovereign kingdom; Capital: Okahao; Common languages: Oshiwambo; Religion: Traditional African religion; Government: Traditional monarchy; Ruler title: Omukwaniilwa; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 1896; Historical region: Ovamboland

name: Qu'aiti Sultanate
label: southern arabia petty kingdoms
description: The Qu'aiti Sultanate was an independent Arabian state founded in the coastal Hadhramaut region of southern Yemen by the influential Qu'aiti family. Utilising wealth and trained mercenary troops accrued from royal service in Hyderabad, the dynasty conquered the port of Ash-Shihr and unified the strategic frankincense and maritime corridors of southern Arabia under their autocratic rule. The sultanate maintained its full sovereign status until 1 May 1888, when its rulers entered into a formal treaty of protection with the British Empire. \n\n Status: Sovereign sultanate; Capital: Ash-Shihr; Common languages: Hadhrami Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Qu'aiti; Ruler title: Sultan; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1859; Disestablished: 1 May 1888; Succeeded by: Aden Protectorate

name: Republic of Haiti
description: The Republic of Haiti was restored as a constitutional republic on 15 January 1859 following the overthrow of Emperor Faustin I by republican forces led by Fabre Geffrard. Administered from Port-au-Prince, the reconstituted government reinstated the 1846 republican constitution, reorganised the national educational system and normalised diplomatic relations with the Holy See through an 1860 concordat. The state preserved its sovereign independence across the western third of Hispaniola despite recurrent domestic revolts and mounting foreign financial indebtedness. \n\n Status: Sovereign republic; Capital: Port-au-Prince; Official languages: French; Common languages: French and Haitian Creole; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Semi-presidential republic; Ruler title: President; Head of state: Fabre Geffrard; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 15 January 1859; Preceded by: Empire of Haiti

name: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia
description: The United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia emerged on 5 February 1859 as a personal union when Alexandru Ioan Cuza was elected as the Domnitor of both Danubian states. Operating under nominal Ottoman suzerainty while maintaining dual legislative bodies in Iași and Bucharest, the embryonic nation enacted sweeping judicial, agrarian and military modernisations to forge a unified national infrastructure. This transitional dual administration formally merged on 3 February 1862 when a single government, national assembly and administrative capital were instituted in Bucharest. \n\n Status: Autonomous personal union under Ottoman vassalage; Capital: Iași and Bucharest; Official languages: Romanian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Constitutional monarchy; Ruler title: Domnitor; Head of state: Alexandru Ioan Cuza; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 5 February 1859; Disestablished: 3 February 1862; Preceded by: Principality of Moldavia and Principality of Wallachia; Succeeded by: Romanian United Principalities

name: Colony of Queensland
label: british colonies in australia
description: The Colony of Queensland was a self-governing British Crown colony established in north-eastern Australia upon its formal separation from New South Wales on 6 June 1859. Governed from the river capital of Brisbane, the colony operated under a bicameral parliament that promoted rapid pastoral expansion, sugarcane cultivation, coastal ports and lucrative gold mining across the tropical north. The colony retained its independent imperial administration until 1 January 1901, when it federated alongside the other Australian colonies to establish the Commonwealth of Australia. \n\n Status: British Crown colony; Capital: Brisbane; Common languages: English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Constitutional monarchy under responsible government; Ruler title: Monarch; First ruler: Victoria; Legislature: Parliament of Queensland; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 6 June 1859; Disestablished: 1 January 1901; Preceded by: Colony of New South Wales; Succeeded by: Commonwealth of Australia

name: Territory of Jefferson
description: The Territory of Jefferson was an unrecognised extralegal territory formed on 24 October 1859 by American pioneers during the height of the Pike's Peak Gold Rush. Operating from Denver City, the provisional government adopted its own constitution, convened an elected General Assembly and established mining courts to manage civic affairs across the Front Range without formal Congressional authorisation. The extralegal administration functioned effectively for sixteen months until yielding peacefully to the newly authorised Territory of Colorado on 28 February 1861. \n\n Status: Unrecognised provisional territory; Capital: Denver; Common languages: English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Provisional territorial democracy; Ruler title: Governor; Head of state: Robert Williamson Steele; Legislature: General Assembly; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 24 October 1859; Disestablished: 28 February 1861; Succeeded by: Colorado Territory

name: United Provinces of Central Italy
description: The United Provinces of Central Italy was a transitional client state established on 8 December 1859 under Piedmontese military auspices in the aftermath of the Second Italian War of Independence. Formed through the union of Tuscany, Parma, Modena and the former Papal Legations, the provisional government operated from Florence to coordinate regional military defence and civil administration. Following overwhelming plebiscites in favour of national unification, the confederation was formally annexed into the Kingdom of Sardinia on 22 March 1860. \n\n Status: Client state (under Sardinia); Capital: Florence; Common languages: Italian; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Provisional military government; Ruler title: Governor-General; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 8 December 1859; Disestablished: 22 March 1860; Preceded by: Grand Duchy of Tuscany; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Sardinia

name: Jandol State
label: indian princely states
description: Jandol State was a small Pashtun princely state situated in the rugged Bajaur and Dir borderlands of the North-West Frontier in present-day Pakistan. Centred on the fortified town of Barwa, the state was ruled by an ambitious Yusufzai chieftaincy, achieving regional military dominance in the late nineteenth century under the celebrated warrior Umra Khan. The realm maintained its internal tribal autonomy under British frontier supervision until being incorporated into the princely state of Dir and subsequently acceding to Pakistan in 1948. \n\n Status: Princely state (under British suzerainty); Capital: Barwa; Common languages: Pashto; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Princely monarchy; Ruler title: Khan; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1860; Disestablished: 1948; Succeeded by: Pakistan; Historical region: North-West Frontier

name: Shonga
description: Shonga was an autonomous riverine chieftaincy situated along the southern banks of the Niger River in present-day Kwara State, western Nigeria. Inhabited primarily by the Nupe people, the town and its surrounding agricultural domains served as an active commercial port for canoe transport, grain distribution and cross-river trade with neighbouring Yoruba communities. The polity maintained its localised self-governance until 1900, when British forces absorbed the Middle Niger kingdoms into the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria. \n\n Status: Sovereign chieftaincy; Capital: Shonga; Common languages: Nupe; Religion: Islam and Traditional African religion; Government: Traditional chieftaincy; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 1860; Disestablished: 1900; Succeeded by: Northern Nigeria Protectorate

name: Mosquito Reserve
description: The Mosquito Reserve was an autonomous indigenous enclave established on 28 January 1860 along the Caribbean littoral of Central America under the Treaty of Managua. Headquartered at the port of Bluefields, the territory was governed by the hereditary Miskito monarch alongside a representative council of indigenous headmen and Creole merchants. While technically under nominal Nicaraguan suzerainty, the reserve functioned with domestic independence until Nicaraguan troops under President José Santos Zelaya militarily occupied and annexed the coast in 1894. \n\n Status: Autonomous indigenous reserve; Capital: Bluefields; Common languages: Miskito, English and Creole; Religion: Moravian Protestantism; Government: Traditional monarchy; Ruler title: Hereditary Chief; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 28 January 1860; Disestablished: 1895; Preceded by: Mosquito Coast; Succeeded by: Nicaragua

name: British Kaffraria
description: British Kaffraria was a distinct British Crown colony established on 7 March 1860 in the eastern frontier region of present-day South Africa between the Keiskamma and Great Kei rivers. Administered from King William's Town by a Lieutenant-Governor, the colony oversaw the subjugation and resettlement of Xhosa communities weakened in the aftermath of the tragic 1856 cattle-killing famine. Confronting continuous financial deficits and administrative redundancy, the territory was formally annexed into the neighbouring Cape Colony on 17 April 1866. \n\n Status: British Crown colony; Capital: King William's Town; Common languages: English, Xhosa and German; Religion: Anglicanism and Protestantism; Government: Colonial administration; Ruler title: Lieutenant-Governor; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 7 March 1860; Disestablished: 17 April 1866; Succeeded by: Cape Colony

name: Territory of Ifni
description: The Territory of Ifni was a Spanish colonial enclave located along the arid Atlantic coastline of south-western Morocco opposite the Canary Islands. Ceded by Morocco under the Treaty of Wad Ras on 26 April 1860, the territory was administered from its coastal capital of Sidi Ifni, developing into a fortified military enclave and regional fisheries hub. Spain maintained direct imperial sovereignty over the coastal strip through the mid-twentieth century until formally retroceding the territory to independent Morocco on 30 June 1969. \n\n Status: Spanish protectorate and colony; Capital: Sidi Ifni; Official languages: Spanish; Common languages: Spanish, Shilha Berber and Moroccan Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam and Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial governorship; Ruler title: Governor-General; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 26 April 1860; Disestablished: 30 June 1969; Succeeded by: Morocco

name: British Concession in Tianjin
label: concessions in china
description: The British Concession in Tianjin was an extraterritorial enclave established on 24 October 1860 along the Hai River following the ratification of the Convention of Beijing. Governed by an elected British Municipal Council alongside consular officials, the settlement developed into northern China's premier commercial, diplomatic and financial emporium, boasting Western-style mansions, banks and modern docks. The concession maintained its administrative autonomy through numerous regional conflicts until it was seized by Japanese military forces on 7 December 1941. \n\n Status: Foreign concession; Administrative seat: Tianjin; Common languages: English and Northern Mandarin; Religion: Christianity; Government: Consular municipal council; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 24 October 1860; Disestablished: 7 December 1941; Succeeded by: Republic of China; Historical region: Concessions in China

name: Kingdom of Araucanía and Patagonia
description: The Kingdom of Araucanía and Patagonia was an unrecognised constitutional monarchy proclaimed on 17 November 1860 in the southern Cone by French lawyer Orélie-Antoine de Tounens. Allied with influential Mapuche chiefs resisting Chilean and Argentine military expansion, Tounens established his royal headquarters at Perquenco and promulgated a national constitution and national flag. The utopian enterprise was brought to an abrupt end on 5 January 1862 when Chilean police captured Tounens, ultimately expelling him from the country as a foreign adventurer. \n\n Status: Unrecognised monarchy; Capital: Perquenco; Common languages: Mapudungun and French; Religion: Traditional Mapuche religion and Christianity; Government: Constitutional monarchy; Ruler title: King; Head of state: Orélie-Antoine I; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 17 November 1860; Disestablished: 5 January 1862; Succeeded by: Chile and Argentina

name: State of South Carolina
label: american confederate secessionist states
description: The State of South Carolina was a short-lived independent republic that functioned between its Ordinance of Secession on 20 December 1860 and the establishment of the Confederacy in February 1861. As the first southern state to withdraw from the United States following Abraham Lincoln's election, the commonwealth asserted complete sovereign independence, organised military defences around Charleston Harbour and dispatched diplomatic commissioners to neighbouring slaveholding states. Its brief period of separate nationhood ended on 4 February 1861 when it became a founding member of the Confederate States of America. \n\n Status: Secessionist republic; Capital: Columbia; Common languages: English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Republic; Ruler title: Governor; Head of state: Francis Wilkinson Pickens; Legislature: General Assembly; Historical era: Late modern; Established: 20 December 1860; Disestablished: 4 February 1861; Succeeded by: Confederate States of America

name: Colony of Rivières du Sud

Following several boundary reductions that carved out Montana and Wyoming, the remaining territory matured into an agricultural and mining powerhouse before achieving statehood in July 1890. \n\n Status: Organised incorporated territory; Capital: Boise; Official languages: English; Common languages: English and indigenous languages; Government: Territorial administration; Ruler title: Governor; Established: 3 March 1863; Disestablished: 3 July 1890; Succeeded by: Idaho

name: United States of Colombia
description: The United States of Colombia was a federal republic established under the Rionegro Constitution following liberal victory in the civil war against conservative centralists. Composed of nine sovereign states encompassing modern Colombia and Panama, the union embraced radical decentralisation, secularised public institutions and promoted unrestricted trade. Recurrent factional conflicts and economic instability eventually led to conservative resurgence under Rafael Nunez, who abolished the federal system in 1886 in favour of the centralised Republic of Colombia. \n\n Status: Federal republic; Capital: Bogota; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Federal presidential republic; Ruler title: President; Established: 8 May 1863; Disestablished: 8 August 1886; Succeeded by: Republic of Colombia

name: Kingdom of Cambodia
description: The Kingdom of Cambodia became a French protectorate in August 1863 when King Norodom signed a treaty in Oudong to safeguard his vulnerable realm against Siamese and Vietnamese domination. French naval officers secured recognition of Cambodia's borders while gradually establishing administrative control over finances, customs collection and external trade. The monarch relocated the royal court to Phnom Penh in 1866, presiding over traditional Buddhist institutions until the protectorate was formally incorporated into the Indochinese Union in 1887. \n\n Status: French protectorate; Capital: Phnom Penh; Common languages: Khmer and French; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Constitutional monarchy under colonial supervision; Ruling dynasty: Varman; Ruler title: King; Established: 11 August 1863; Succeeded by: French Indochina

name: Dominican Republic
description: The Dominican Republic regained its national sovereignty through the Dominican Restoration War, which commenced in September 1863 and decisively ended Spanish recolonisation across eastern Hispaniola. Governed from the historic capital of Santo Domingo, the republic established a presidential constitutional system that contended with intense political factionalism and mounting external debts. The country preserved its independent statehood through periods of foreign financial receivership and military intervention, developing into a major Caribbean agrarian and commercial economy. \n\n Status: Sovereign republic; Capital and largest city: Santo Domingo; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Congress; Historical era: Modern era; Reorganised: 1 September 1863; Currency: Dominican peso

name: Shanghai International Settlement
label: concessions in china
description: The Shanghai International Settlement emerged in September 1863 through the formal amalgamation of the British and American concessions along the Huangpu River. Administered by the multinational Shanghai Municipal Council, the enclave functioned as an autonomous mercantile city-state protected by extraterritorial privileges, its own police force and volunteer corps. The settlement transformed into Asia's premier financial and trading hub until imperial Japanese forces crossed Suzhou Creek to occupy the district upon the outbreak of the Pacific War. \n\n Status: Extraterritorial settlement; Administrative seat: Shanghai; Official languages: English; Common languages: English and Shanghainese; Government: Municipal council; Historical era: Late Qing to Republic; Established: 21 September 1863; Disestablished: 8 December 1941; Preceded by: British and American concessions

name: Free State of Jones
description: The Free State of Jones was an insurgent Unionist enclave formed in Jones County, Mississippi, by Confederate deserters and local anti-secessionists under the leadership of Newton Knight. Rejecting the authority of the Confederate government in protest of onerous taxes and conscription laws, the Knight Company conducted guerrilla warfare against regular troops across the regional pine forests and swamps. The independent band maintained practical control over the county seat of Ellisville until federal authority was restored at the close of the American Civil War. \n\n Status: Insurgent republic; Administrative seat: Ellisville; Common languages: English; Religion: Protestantism; Government: Autonomous rebel administration; Head of state: Newton Knight; Historical era: American Civil War; Established: 13 October 1863; Disestablished: 30 November 1865

name: German Confederation (Military Occupation)
description: The German Confederation military occupation of the Duchies of Holstein and Lauenburg commenced on 23 December 1863 as a federal execution mandated by the Diet in Frankfurt. Deployed to challenge Danish constitutional integration of the duchies, Saxon and Hanoverian troops under Confederate authority secured administrative control over the regional infrastructure. This military intervention directly precipitated the Second Schleswig War, leading to joint Austro-Prussian operations and the formal transfer of the duchies through the Treaty of Vienna in October 1864. \n\n Status: Federal military occupation; Administrative seat: Frankfurt; Common languages: German and Danish; Religion: Lutheranism; Government: Federal execution military command; Historical era: German unification; Established: 23 December 1863; Disestablished: 30 October 1864; Succeeded by: Condominium of Austria and Prussia

name: Sultanate of Witu
description: The Sultanate of Witu was an independent Swahili state established on the northern Kenyan littoral by Ahmad ibn Fumo Bakari after his expulsion from the Pate archipelago. Operating from the forested stronghold of Witu inland from Lamu, the sultan offered asylum to runaway slaves and forged a formidable military resistance against the aggressive encroachment of Zanzibar. The sultanate maintained its political independence and maritime trade networks until accepting an imperial German protectorate in April 1885. \n\n Status: Sovereign sultanate; Capital: Witu; Common languages: Swahili and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy; Ruler title: Sultan; Historical era: Pre-colonial East Africa; Established: 1864; Succeeded by: German Wituland

name: Mexican Empire
description: The Mexican Empire was a monarchical regime established under French military sponsorship and supported by Mexican conservative factions during the Second French Intervention. Austrian Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg accepted the imperial crown in April 1864, reigning from Chapultepec Castle in Mexico City while introducing moderate liberal legal codes and educational reforms. However, the regime remained heavily dependent on French expeditionary forces, collapsing rapidly when French troops withdrew and Republican armies under Benito Juarez captured and executed the emperor at Queretaro. \n\n Status: Client monarchy; Capital: Mexico City; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Habsburg-Lorraine; Ruler title: Emperor; Established: 10 April 1864; Disestablished: 19 June 1867; Preceded by: Second Mexican Republic

name: Territory of Montana
description: The Territory of Montana was an organised incorporated possession of the United States formed from the northeastern portion of Idaho Territory following major mineral discoveries along Grasshopper and Alder creeks. Successive gold and silver rushes attracted thousands of miners, shifting the territorial capital from Bannack to Virginia City and ultimately to Helena in 1875. The territory developed extensive cattle ranching across its eastern plains and expanded rail networks before achieving statehood as the forty-first state of the Union in November 1889. \n\n Status: Organised incorporated territory; Capital: Helena; Official languages: English; Common languages: English and indigenous languages; Government: Territorial administration; Ruler title: Governor; Established: 26 May 1864; Disestablished: 8 November 1889; Succeeded by: Montana

name: Oriental State of Uruguay
description: The Oriental State of Uruguay during this tumultuous phase functioned as the constitutional government controlled by the National Blanco Party under Bernardo Berro and Atanasio Cruz Aguirre amidst the Uruguayan War. Operating without a secure capital as Colorado insurgents and Brazilian imperial forces besieged provincial strongholds, Blanco authorities conducted armed resistance across the rural departments. The administration sought military assistance from Paraguayan leader Francisco Solano Lopez before collapsing with the fall of Montevideo in February 1865. \n\n Status: Embattled constitutional republic; Administrative seat: Mobile administration; Common languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Presidential republic; Head of state: Atanasio Cruz Aguirre; Historical era: Uruguayan War; Established: 14 October 1864; Disestablished: 20 February 1865

name: Colorados
description: The Colorados constituted an insurgent political and military movement led by General Venancio Flores during the decisive phase of the Uruguayan War of 1864 to 1865. Supported by covert Argentine logistics and an overt military alliance with the Empire of Brazil, the Colorado army swept across the Uruguayan countryside to overthrow the governing Blanco regime. Upon capturing key departmental fortresses and entering Montevideo in February 1865, Flores established a provisional military government that aligned the republic with the Triple Alliance. \n\n Status: Insurgent revolutionary faction; Administrative seat: Mobile military headquarters; Common languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Military junta; Head of state: Venancio Flores; Historical era: Uruguayan War; Established: 24 October 1864; Disestablished: 20 February 1865

name: Condominium of Austria and Prussia
label: german confederation
description: The Condominium of Austria and Prussia was a joint military and civil administration established over the Elbe duchies of Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg following Denmark's defeat in the Second Schleswig War. Mandated by the Treaty of Vienna in October 1864, the two German powers governed the territories concurrently while contending over competing visions for their permanent constitutional status. This uneasy dual rule proved unworkable and was terminated by the Gastein Convention of August 1865, which partitioned administrative control between the co-rulers. \n\n Status: Dual military condominium; Administrative seat: Schleswig; Common languages: German and Danish; Religion: Lutheranism; Government: Joint civil-military commission; Historical era: German unification; Established: 30 October 1864; Disestablished: 14 August 1865; Succeeded by: Gastein Convention partition

name: Brazil and Colorados
description: The Brazil and Colorados alliance was a combined expeditionary force formed between the imperial armed forces of Brazil and Venancio Flores' Uruguayan rebel army during the Uruguayan War. Operating along the Uruguay River and interior departments, this military coalition laid siege to Paysandu and systematically dismantled the fortified strongholds of the governing Blanco forces. Their joint victory culminated in the capture of Montevideo in February 1865, successfully installing Flores as president and paving the way for the broader Triple Alliance against Paraguay. \n\n Status: Military coalition; Administrative seat: Mobile command; Common languages: Portuguese and Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Allied military command; Historical era: Uruguayan War; Established: 28 November 1864; Disestablished: 20 February 1865; Succeeded by: Provisional Government of Uruguay

name: Republic of Paraguay (Military Occupation)
description: The Republic of Paraguay military occupation encompassed territories in Brazilian Mato Grosso and Argentine Corrientes seized by Paraguayan armies in the opening stages of the Paraguayan War. Under the strategic direction of President Francisco Solano Lopez, Paraguayan garrisons requisitioned livestock, dismantled regional river defences and established provisional martial administration across captured river ports. Sustained counter-offensives by allied Brazilian, Argentine and Uruguayan forces gradually dislodged the occupying troops, forcing Paraguay into a desperate defensive retreat onto its own soil. \n\n Status: Military occupation zone; Administrative seat: Mobile military command; Common languages: Guarani and Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Military occupation administration; Head of state: Francisco Solano Lopez; Historical era: Paraguayan War; Established: 29 December 1864; Disestablished: 1 July 1867

name: Baria State
label: indian princely states
description: Baria State was a princely realm located in the hilly tract of Gujarat under the Rewa Kantha Agency of the Bombay Presidency during the British Raj. Ruled by the Khichi Chauhan clan of Rajputs from their capital at Devgadh Baria, the state maintained internal governance while acknowledging British paramountcy. The rulers modernised local communication routes, constructed a dedicated narrow-gauge railway and fostered agriculture until formally acceding to the Union of India following independence in 1948. \n\n Status: Princely state; Capital: Devgadh Baria; Common languages: Gujarati and Hindi; Religion: Hinduism; Government: Princely monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Chauhan Rajput; Ruler title: Maharaol; Historical era: British Raj; Succeeded by: India

name: Black Flag Army
description: The Black Flag Army was an autonomous military faction established in Upper Tonkin by Liu Yongfu and former Taiping and Zhuang irregulars who crossed the Chinese frontier in 1865. Headquartered at the fortified river post of Baosheng along the upper Red River, the band exerted territorial control over trade routes and collected river tolls under nominal recognition from the Vietnamese imperial court. Their hardened rifle units played a celebrated role in confronting French colonial expeditions until official suppression and incorporation during the Sino-French War. \n\n Status: Autonomous military band; Capital: Baosheng; Common languages: Zhuang, Cantonese and Vietnamese; Religion: Chinese folk religion and Confucianism; Government: Military chieftaincy; Ruler title: Commander; Head of state: Liu Yongfu; Established: 1865; Disestablished: 1 July 1884

name: Ili Sultanate
description: The Ili Sultanate was an independent Islamic state formed in the Kulja region of northern Xinjiang during the widespread Dungan Revolt against the Qing dynasty. Local Turkic Muslims and Hui rebels overwhelmed the imperial Manchu garrisons in 1865, establishing a sovereign administration based at Ghulja under Sultan Eliya Hazret and subsequent warlords. Entangled in fierce factional warfare and regional rivalries with neighbouring nomadic groups, the sultanate was ultimately occupied and annexed by the Russian Empire in 1871 to forestall border instability. \n\n Status: Rebel Islamic sultanate; Capital: Ghulja; Common languages: Chagatai and Mandarin Chinese; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Theocratic monarchy; Ruler title: Sultan; Historical era: Dungan Revolt; Established: 1865; Disestablished: 1872; Succeeded by: Russian Turkestan

name: Kontagora Emirate
label: fula jihads polities
description: The Kontagora Emirate was a martial Islamic polity founded in north-central Nigeria by Umaru Nagwamatse, a prince of the Sokoto Caliphate, during the later Fula jihads. Carved out through extensive military raiding across the Niger river basin, the emirate established its walled capital at Kontagora and imposed tribute over surrounding indigenous populations. Famous for its cavalry forces, the state maintained fierce independence until British troops under Frederick Lugard stormed Kontagora in January 1901, incorporating the emirate into the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria. \n\n Status: Islamic emirate; Capital: Kontagora; Common languages: Hausa and Fula; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Islamic emirate; Ruling dynasty: Toronkawa; Ruler title: Sarkin Sudan; Established: 1865; Disestablished: 31 January 1901; Succeeded by: Northern Nigeria Protectorate

name: United States of Venezuela
description: The United States of Venezuela was the official federal designation of the Venezuelan nation established under the 1864 constitution promulgated by President Juan Crisostomo Falcon following the Federal War. Comprising autonomous regional states coordinated from Caracas, the republic weathered decades of caudillo rebellions, economic modernisation fuelled by early petroleum exploitation and military dictatorships. The country retained its federal constitutional structure until April 1953, when a new charter reorganised the state as the Republic of Venezuela. \n\n Status: Federal republic; Capital: Caracas; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Federal presidential republic; Ruler title: President; Established: 1865; Disestablished: 11 April 1953; Succeeded by: Republic of Venezuela

name: Yengan State
label: shan states
description: Yengan State was a small upland Shan principality lying in the Myelat division of the Shan Hills that owed vassalage and tributary services to the Burmese Konbaung monarchy. Ruled from the township of Yengan by a traditional ngwegunhmu, the domain supervised terraced agriculture, cattle breeding and regional caravan routes connecting the Shan plateau to the Irrawaddy basin. The principality preserved its customary feudal governance until British annexation of Upper Burma dissolved Burmese suzerainty and brought the territory under colonial administration. \n\n Status: Tributary princely state; Capital: Yengan; Common languages: Danu, Shan and Burmese; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Hereditary princedom; Ruler title: Ngwegunhmu; Historical era: Konbaung dynasty; Established: 1865; Succeeded by: British Burma

name: Restoring Army
description: The Restoring Army was an insurrectionary military movement launched in Arequipa by Colonel Mariano Ignacio Prado to oppose the unpopular Vivanco-Pareja Treaty signed with Spain. Mobilising widespread national indignation against Spanish naval aggression and government concessions, Prado's forces seized control of southern Peru and advanced rapidly toward Lima. The revolutionary army overthrew President Juan Antonio Pezet in November 1865, allowing Prado to assume dictatorial executive authority and declare outright war against the Spanish squadron. \n\n Status: Revolutionary military movement; Administrative seat: Mobile command; Common languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Provisional military administration; Head of state: Mariano Ignacio Prado; Historical era: Chincha Islands War; Established: 28 February 1865; Disestablished: 8 November 1865

name: Indian Territory
description: The Indian Territory under Confederate alignment held out during the closing weeks of the American Civil War after the fall of Richmond, maintaining allegiance to the Southern cause under Brigadier General Stand Watie. Governed administratively from Armstrong Academy within the Choctaw Nation, this autonomous territory encompassed allied tribal nations including factions of the Cherokee, Creek, Seminole, Choctaw and Chickasaw. Watie became the final Confederate general to lay down arms, surrendering his Native American battalions at Doaksville on 23 June 1865. \n\n Status: Confederate allied territory; Administrative seat: Armstrong Academy; Common languages: English, Cherokee, Choctaw and Muscogee; Religion: Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Autonomous tribal confederacy; Ruler title: Principal Chief; Historical era: American Civil War; Established: 13 May 1865; Disestablished: 13 June 1865

name: Bhutan
description: Bhutan was a Himalayan Buddhist state that came under indirect British imperial influence following its defeat in the Duar War and the signing of the Treaty of Sinchula in November 1865. Ceding the fertile Assam and Bengal Duars in exchange for an annual subsidy, the kingdom maintained its traditional dual system of spiritual and secular governance divided between the Je Khenpo and the Druk Desi. Decentralised penlops dominated provincial politics from regional dzongs until Ugyen Wangchuck consolidated power, founding the hereditary Wangchuck monarchy in 1907. \n\n Status: British protectorate; Capital: Thimphu and Punakha; Common languages: Dzongkha; Religion: Vajrayana Buddhism; Government: Dual system of religious and secular rule; Head of state: Druk Desi; Historical era: Late pre-monarchical Bhutan; Established: 11 November 1865; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Bhutan

name: American Trading Company of Borneo
description: The American Trading Company of Borneo was a commercial enterprise established by American merchants Joseph William Torrey and Thomas Bradley Harris after acquiring land concessions from the Sultan of Brunei in 1865. Operating from a pioneer trading settlement named Ellena near Kimanis in northern Borneo, the company sought to exploit timber and tropical agriculture while Torrey styled himself Rajah of Ambong and Marudu. Beset by financial collapse, disease and labour unrest, the company abandoned its colonial settlement, eventually selling its territorial claims to Baron von Overbeck in 1878. \n\n Status: Commercial chartered colony; Administrative seat: Kimanis; Official languages: English; Common languages: English, Malay and Chinese; Government: Chartered company administration; Head of state: Joseph William Torrey; Historical era: Victorian era; Established: 1866; Disestablished: 1878

name: Chhuikhadan State
label: indian princely states
description: Chhuikhadan State was an Indian princely state situated in the Chhattisgarh region, ruled by the Bairagi Mahant dynasty under the Central Provinces Agency of the British Raj. Formal recognition by British colonial authorities in 1865 established the hereditary rulers as feudatory chiefs over more than one hundred agrarian villages centred around Chhuikhadan. The princely domain retained internal autonomy over judicial and fiscal matters until its rulers signed the instrument of accession to the Dominion of India in January 1948. \n\n Status: Princely state; Capital: Chhuikhadan; Common languages: Chhattisgarhi and Hindi; Religion: Hinduism; Government: Princely monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Bairagi; Ruler title: Mahant; Historical era: British Raj; Succeeded by: India

name: Nandgaon State
label: indian princely states
description: Nandgaon State was a princely domain in central India ruled by Vaishnav Bairagi Mahants under the Chhattisgarh States Agency during the era of British paramountcy. Emerging from eighteenth-century Maratha grants, the state received formal sanad recognition from the British Crown in 1865, securing dynastic succession and internal fiscal control. The rulers developed Rajnandgaon into a flourishing regional commercial hub with modern cotton mills, schools and grain markets before peacefully merging into the Indian Union in 1948. \n\n Status: Princely state; Capital: Rajnandgaon; Common languages: Chhattisgarhi and Hindi; Religion: Hinduism; Government: Princely monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Bairagi; Ruler title: Mahant Raja Bahadur; Historical era: British Raj; Succeeded by: India

name: Yettishar
description: Yettishar, commonly known as Kashgaria or the Kashgar Emirate, was a sovereign Muslim state that dominated the Tarim Basin of southern Xinjiang during the Dungan Revolt. Founded by the Kokandi commander Yakub Beg, who captured the seven historic oasis cities including Kashgar, Khotan and Yarkand, the state established strict Islamic governance and concluded diplomatic treaties with Britain and Russia. After the Ottoman Empire recognised Yakub Beg as emir in 1873, the realm maintained independent power until Qing imperial forces under Zuo Zongtang reconquered the region in late 1877. \n\n Status: Sovereign Islamic emirate; Capital: Kashgar; Common languages: Chagatai and Persian; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Islamic absolute monarchy; Ruler title: Emir; Head of state: Yakub Beg; Established: 1866; Disestablished: 25 December 1877

name: Triple Alliance (Military Occupation)
description: The Triple Alliance military occupation held extensive tracts of Paraguayan territory following the allied amphibious crossing of the Parana River in April 1866 during the Paraguayan War. Joint Brazilian, Argentine and Uruguayan army headquarters coordinated frontline logistics, established martial garrisons in captured fortifications like Humaita and subsequently occupied the devastated capital of Asuncion in 1869. The allied coalition maintained an armed occupational presence and supervised a provisional Paraguayan administration until final peace treaties and border adjustments were settled in the late 1870s. \n\n Status: Joint military occupation; Administrative seat: Mobile allied headquarters; Common languages: Portuguese and Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Allied military administration; Historical era: Paraguayan War; Established: 16 April 1866; Disestablished: 1877; Succeeded by: Republic of Paraguay

name: Kingdom of Italy (Military Occupation)
description: The Kingdom of Italy military occupation encompassed contested frontier zones occupied by the Royal Italian Army during operational campaigns across the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Beginning with the liberation and martial administration of Venetian territories during the Third Italian War of Independence in 1866, Italian military commands supervised civilian transport, garrisoned strategic fortresses and maintained public order. Similar temporary occupation administrations were instituted during overseas colonial campaigns in the Horn of Africa and the Aegean Sea before permanent civilian treaties took effect. \n\n Status: Military occupation administration; Administrative seat: Mobile military command; Official languages: Italian; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Military command; Historical era: Italian unification to World War II; Established: 11 July 1866; Disestablished: 9 September 1943; Preceded by: Austrian Empire

name: Isle of Man
description: The Isle of Man is an internally self-governing Crown dependency in the Irish Sea whose constitutional status was revitalised by fiscal reforms and popular elections to the House of Keys in 1866 and 1867. Operating under the ancient parliamentary assembly of Tynwald, the island shifted its principal administrative functions from Castletown to Douglas during the late Victorian era. While the British Crown retains responsibility for external defence and diplomatic representation, the insular government preserves distinct legal traditions, financial autonomy and ancient customary rights. \n\n Status: British Crown dependency; Capital: Douglas; Official languages: English and Manx; Religion: Christianity; Government: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Legislature: Tynwald; Historical era: Late modern era; Reorganised: 1867; Currency: Manx pound

name: Khanate of Kokand
description: The Khanate of Kokand was reduced to a vassal protectorate of the Russian Empire in 1867 after Tsarist forces overran Tashkent and the northern Fergana frontiers. Khudayar Khan governed a truncated realm from the city of Kokand, compelled to sign unequal commercial treaties, pay heavy indemnities and tolerate Russian garrisons along the Syr Darya. Escalating popular outrage and widespread peasant rebellions prompted direct Russian military intervention in early 1876, resulting in the formal abolition of the khanate and its conversion into Fergana Oblast. \n\n Status: Russian protectorate; Capital: Kokand; Common languages: Chagatai Turkic and Persian; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Ming; Ruler title: Khan; Established: 1 February 1867; Disestablished: 1 February 1876; Succeeded by: Russian Empire

name: Principality of Serbia
description: The Principality of Serbia secured de facto sovereign independence on 18 April 1867 when the final Ottoman garrisons evacuated the citadel of Belgrade and other fortress towns across the country. Guided by Prince Mihailo Obrenovic and later Milan IV, the Balkan state developed regular armed forces, expanded domestic administrative ministries and fostered national political parties. Following the Great Eastern Crisis and territorial gains ratified by the Congress of Berlin, Serbia achieved formal international recognition before elevating itself to a kingdom in 1882. \n\n Status: Autonomous principality; Capital: Belgrade; Official languages: Serbian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Obrenovic; Ruler title: Prince; Established: 18 April 1867; Disestablished: 6 March 1882; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Serbia

name: Khedivate of Egypt
description: The Khedivate of Egypt was established on 8 June 1867 when Sultan Abdulaziz formally granted Isma'il Pasha the hereditary title of Khedive, conferring comprehensive internal autonomy within the Ottoman Empire. Operating from Cairo, the Egyptian administration launched vast modernisation schemes, expanded territorial control southwards along the Red Sea and completed the monumental Suez Canal. Massive foreign borrowing nevertheless created crippling financial crises, leading to Anglo-French dual control and ultimately the 1882 British military occupation following the nationalist Urabi revolt. \n\n Status: Autonomous Ottoman khedivate; Capital: Cairo; Common languages: Arabic and Ottoman Turkish; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Hereditary constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Muhammad Ali; Ruler title: Khedive; Established: 8 June 1867; Disestablished: 1 October 1882

name: Austro-Hungarian Monarchy
description: The Austro-Hungarian Monarchy was a Central European dual monarchy formed through the Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867 following Austria's defeat in the Austro-Prussian War. Binding the Austrian Empire and the Kingdom of Hungary under the common sceptre of Emperor-King Franz Joseph I, the real union maintained shared foreign, military and financial ministries alongside distinct national parliaments in Vienna and Budapest. The multinational empire flourished as a major industrial and cultural powerhouse until centrifugal ethnic tensions and military collapse in the First World War precipitated its partition. \n\n Status: Sovereign dual monarchy; Capital: Vienna and Budapest; Common languages: German and Hungarian; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Constitutional dual monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Habsburg-Lorraine; Head of state: Emperor-King; Established: 12 June 1867; Disestablished: 12 November 1918

name: United Mexican States
description: The United Mexican States restored its republican constitutional order on 19 June 1867 following the overthrow and execution of Emperor Maximilian by triumphant liberal armies under Benito Juarez. Centred in Mexico City, the restored republic implemented the secularising principles of the 1857 Constitution, consolidated national borders and initiated extensive transport and educational improvements. Under the long presidency of Porfirio Diaz, the federation experienced substantial industrial expansion and foreign investment, establishing the administrative foundations of the modern North American nation. \n\n Status: Sovereign federal republic; Capital and largest city: Mexico City; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Federal presidential republic; Legislature: Congress of the Union; Historical era: Restored Republic to Modern era; Reorganised: 19 June 1867; Currency: Mexican peso

name: Dominion of Canada
description: The Dominion of Canada was established on 1 July 1867 under the British North America Act, uniting the provinces of Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick into a self-governing federal polity. Headquartered in Ottawa, the confederation expanded rapidly across the northern half of North America by incorporating Rupert's Land, British Columbia and Prince Edward Island while constructing a transcontinental railway. Canada assumed steadily greater autonomy over domestic governance and foreign affairs, culminating in full legislative equality under the Statute of Westminster in 1931. \n\n Status: British dominion; Capital: Ottawa; Official languages: English and French; Religion: Christianity; Government: Federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Ruler title: Governor General; Legislature: Parliament; Established: 1 July 1867; Disestablished: 11 December 1931; Succeeded by: Canada

name: Republic of Peru
description: The Republic of Peru during this brief revolutionary interlude was claimed by constitutionalist insurgent forces led by General Pedro Diez Canseco in Arequipa and Colonel Jose Balta in Chiclayo. Opposing the newly promulgated 1867 constitution as an illegitimate centralist imposition by President Mariano Ignacio Prado, the insurrectionists established provincial rebel directorates and mobilised civic militias. Their coordinated military pressure compelled Prado to resign and flee into exile in January 1868, restoring the conservative charter of 1860 under a provisional government. \n\n Status: Insurgent constitutionalist faction; Administrative seat: Mobile command; Common languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Provisional revolutionary administration; Head of state: Pedro Diez Canseco; Historical era: Peruvian Civil War of 1867; Established: 11 September 1867; Disestablished: 22 January 1868

name: Department of Alaska
description: The Department of Alaska was the initial administrative designation for the vast subarctic expanse purchased by the United States from the Russian Empire in October 1867. Governed from the coastal settlement of Sitka successively by the United States Army, the Department of the Treasury and the United States Navy, the territory lacked organised civilian courts and local municipal representation. Military and revenue officers maintained basic order among indigenous communities and maritime traders until Congress passed the First Organic Act in 1884, establishing the civil District of Alaska. \n\n Status: Unorganised military-administered territory; Capital: Sitka; Official languages: English; Common languages: English, Russian, Tlingit and Aleut; Government: Military and naval administration; Ruler title: Military commander; Established: 18 October 1867; Disestablished: 17 May 1884; Succeeded by: District of Alaska

name: Kingdom of Rapa
description: The Kingdom of Rapa was an isolated Polynesian realm centred on the mountainous island of Rapa Iti in the Austral archipelago that accepted a French protectorate in 1868. Governed by indigenous hereditary monarchs from the harbour settlement of Ahurei, the insular community maintained traditional agricultural terracing and communal governance while facing catastrophic depopulation caused by foreign epidemics and Peruvian slave raids. French colonial authorities oversaw maritime commerce and island affairs until formally annexing Rapa into the Oceanic establishments of French Polynesia in 1881. \n\n Status: French protectorate; Capital: Ahurei; Common languages: Rapa and French; Religion: Protestantism and traditional beliefs; Government: Traditional monarchy; Ruler title: King; Historical era: Scramble for Oceania; Established: 1868; Disestablished: 6 March 1881; Succeeded by: French Polynesia

name: Lawa Thikana
label: indian princely states
description: Lawa Thikana was a compact princely chiefship in Rajasthan ruled by the Dasawat Naruka clan of Rajputs under the direct oversight of the Rajputana Agency. Originally subordinate to the Nawab of Tonk, the estate declared its independence following violent border clashes in 1867, prompting British authorities to elevate Lawa to a separate feudatory domain in 1868. The thakur administered the fortified town of Lawa and surrounding villages with domestic judicial autonomy until joining the Matsya Union and subsequent integration into independent India. \n\n Status: Princely chiefship; Capital: Lawa; Common languages: Rajasthani and Hindi; Religion: Hinduism; Government: Princely estate; Ruling dynasty: Naruka Rajput; Ruler title: Thakur; Historical era: British Raj; Succeeded by: India

name: Republic of Manitobah
description: The Republic of Manitobah was an unrecognised pioneer settler state established near Portage la Prairie outside the legal boundaries of the Red River Colony by Thomas Spence. Seeking to organise civic governance, build municipal infrastructure and levy local taxes beyond the effective jurisdiction of the Hudson's Bay Company, Spence and his council drafted a local constitution. The British Colonial Office refused official recognition, warning that collecting taxes without authority was unlawful, and the administration collapsed shortly before the creation of Manitoba in 1870. \n\n Status: Unrecognised settler republic; Capital: Portage la Prairie; Common languages: English and Metis French; Religion: Protestantism; Government: Provisional republic; Head of state: Thomas Spence; Historical era: Canadian Confederation era; Established: 1868; Disestablished: 12 May 1870; Succeeded by: Manitoba

name: Imperial Faction
description: The Imperial Faction comprised the formidable political and military coalition of samurai domains, led by Satsuma, Choshu and Tosa, fighting to restore supreme temporal governance to Emperor Meiji during the Boshin War. Mobilising modernised infantry and Western rifled artillery under Saigo Takamori and imperial prince Arisugawa Taruhito, the allied forces crushed the Tokugawa shogunate at Toba-Fushimi and captured Edo Castle. The faction successfully suppressed regional samurai confederacies in northern Honshu, clearing the path for the centralised administrative transformation of Meiji Japan. \n\n Status: Revolutionary military coalition; Administrative seat: Kyoto and Edo; Common languages: Japanese; Religion: Shinto and Buddhism; Government: Imperial military coalition; Head of state: Emperor Meiji; Historical era: Bakumatsu to Meiji Restoration; Established: 31 January 1868; Disestablished: 7 November 1868

name: Emirate of Bukhara
description: The Emirate of Bukhara became an autonomous protectorate of the Russian Empire following its military defeat at Zerabulak and the subsequent treaty signed in May 1868. Governed by the Manghit dynasty from the historic oasis city of Bukhara, the emir preserved domestic theocratic authority, Islamic courts and traditional taxation across Transoxiana while surrendering foreign policy to Russian residency officials. The protectorate survived through the late imperial period until Bolshevik forces and revolutionary Young Bukharans overthrew the last emir, Alim Khan, in October 1920. \n\n Status: Russian protectorate; Capital: Bukhara; Common languages: Persian and Chagatai Turkic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute theocratic monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Manghit; Ruler title: Emir; Established: 20 May 1868; Disestablished: 8 October 1920; Succeeded by: Bukharan People's Soviet Republic

name: Territory of Wyoming
description: The Territory of Wyoming was an organised incorporated territory of the United States carved from parts of the Dakota, Idaho and Utah territories to accommodate rapid settlement along the Union Pacific Railroad. Governed from the booming railway boomtown of Cheyenne, the territory enacted historic legislation in 1869 that granted women full voting and office-holding rights for the first time in the nation. Bolstered by expansive open-range cattle ranching and coal mining operations, Wyoming achieved permanent admission into the Union as the forty-fourth state in 1890. \n\n Status: Organised incorporated territory; Capital: Cheyenne; Official languages: English; Common languages: English and Shoshone; Government: Territorial administration; Ruler title: Governor; Established: 25 July 1868; Disestablished: 10 July 1890; Succeeded by: Wyoming

name: Cuban Rebels
description: The Cuban Rebels constituted the insurgent movement for national liberation initiated by Carlos Manuel de Cespedes on 10 October 1868 with the Cry of Yara and the proclamation of the Republic of Cuba in Arms. Operating from the liberated city of Bayamo and interior mountain strongholds in Oriente and Camaguey, the insurgent mambises waged a bitter ten-year guerrilla campaign against Spanish colonial forces. Armed resistance across the island persisted through multiple insurgent waves, reviving national liberation struggles until final victory over Spanish authority in 1898. \n\n Status: Revolutionary liberation government; Capital: Bayamo; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Provisional insurgent republic; Ruler title: President of the Republic in Arms; First ruler: Carlos Manuel de Cespedes; Established: 13 October 1868; Disestablished: 28 May 1878

name: Nicobar Islands
description: The Nicobar Islands were acquired as a British colonial possession in October 1868 following formal negotiations that transferred sovereign rights from Denmark, which had abandoned its failed settlement attempts. Centred on the strategic natural harbour of Nancowry in the eastern Indian Ocean, the British administration established a naval monitoring station and penal outpost to suppress regional piracy. The islands were placed under the superintendence of Port Blair, being rapidly integrated into the administrative structure of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands penal settlement. \n\n Status: British crown colony; Administrative seat: Nancowry; Official languages: English; Common languages: Nicobarese, English and Hindi; Government: Colonial penal administration; Historical era: Victorian era; Established: 16 October 1868; Disestablished: 1870; Succeeded by: Chief Commissionership of Andaman and Nicobar Islands

name: German Factories in Cameroon
description: The German Factories in Cameroon were commercial trading posts established along the Wouri River estuary by prominent mercantile houses from the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, including C. Woermann and Jantzen & Thormahlen. Headquartered at Douala, these coastal factories conducted lucrative trade in palm oil, timber and ivory with local Duala chiefs under the municipal protection of Hamburg. The establishments operated as autonomous commercial enclaves until the unification of Germany in January 1871 brought Hamburg and its overseas mercantile ventures under imperial supervision. \n\n Status: Commercial trading enclave; Administrative seat: Douala; Common languages: German, Duala and English; Religion: Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Corporate trading agency; Historical era: Pre-colonial West Africa; Established: 1869; Disestablished: 18 January 1871; Succeeded by: German Reich

name: Gomoa
description: Gomoa was a sovereign Akan state on the coastal littoral of southern Ghana, divided into the twin chiefdoms of Gomoa Assin and Gomoa Ajumako with a major maritime outlet at Apam. Allied with the Fante Confederacy, the polity coordinated regional commercial trade in palm products and salt while defending its borders against Asante military incursions. Traditional chiefs and local councils managed communal justice and coastal fisheries until British colonial authorities gradually dismantled indigenous sovereignty, integrating Gomoa into the Gold Coast Colony in 1902. \n\n Status: Sovereign Akan kingdom; Capital: Apam; Common languages: Akan and Fante; Religion: Traditional Akan religion and Christianity; Government: Traditional chiefdom council; Ruler title: Omanhene; Historical era: Pre-colonial Gold Coast; Established: 1869; Disestablished: 1902; Succeeded by: Gold Coast Colony

name: Republic of Ezo
